# DISCOVERSE: ROCm data generation, training, and multi-view videos

DISCOVERSE is a simulation framework for Real2Sim2Real robot learning, covering AIRBOT, MMK2, expert state machines, imitation learning, LiDAR, and 3DGS. This chapter begins with source code and model downloading, followed by expert data generation, LeRobot conversion, ACT/Diffusion Policy training, closed loop evaluation, and three-channel high-definition video.

## Output of this chapter

- AIRBOT and MMK2 scenario operation records;
- Successful expert trajectory and round-by-round generation lists;
- LeRobot dataset, action/observation mapping, and replay videos;
- ACT or Diffusion Policy model, closed loop results, and multi-view videos;
- Optional 3DGS dynamic rendering.

Record the upstream version after installation:

```bash
git -C "$SRC_ROOT/DISCOVERSE" rev-parse HEAD
```

## 1. Download and Install

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT"
git lfs install
git clone https://github.com/discoverse-dev/DISCOVERSE.git
cd DISCOVERSE

export DISCOVERSE_ENV="$ENV_ROOT/discoverse-rocm"
python3.10 -m venv "$DISCOVERSE_ENV"
source "$DISCOVERSE_ENV/bin/activate"
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e .
python scripts/setup_submodules.py
python scripts/check_installation.py
```

Add dependencies according to the purpose:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[act_full]'
python -m pip install -e '.[lidar,visualization]'
python -m pip install -e '.[gs]'
```

3DGS [Three-Dimensional Gaussian Spill] model is provided by `tatp/DISCOVERSE-models`. It will be automatically downloaded during the first run, or you can log in in advance:

```bash
hf auth login
```

## 2. Basic Operation Check

```bash
export MUJOCO_GL=egl
python discoverse/robots_env/airbot_play_base.py
python discoverse/robots_env/mmk2_base.py

python examples/mocap_ik/mocap_ik_manipulator.py \
  -r airbot_play \
  -t place_block \
  --record \
  --camera-names global_camera wrist_camera
```

The migration acceptance covers 18 operational checks, 12 AIRBOT tasks, and 8 MMK2 fixed scenarios. After the basic checks are passed, training data is generated.

## 3. Expert Trajectory Generation

The official task script already includes the expert state machine. Take the AIRBOT placement blocks as an example:

```bash
python examples/tasks_airbot_play/place_block.py --help
```

The expert state machine must satisfy both kinematic and physical constraints. When IK [inverse kinematics] unreachable occurs, first check whether the target pose exceeds the robotic arm’s working space, whether the end pose causes joint limits, and whether there are pose jumps between adjacent states. For stacking tasks, the expert path is divided into pre-grasping, grasping, lifting, pre-placement, lowering, release, and evacuation, and interpolation is applied for adjacent states. When a supporting object is knocked over, adjust the approach and evacuation directions; no path correction is achieved by increasing mass.

The parameter names may vary across different versions. For now, use `--help`. When generating in bulk, fix the data root directory, seed range, and target success count:

```bash
export DISCOVERSE_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT/discoverse"
mkdir -p "$DISCOVERSE_DATA_ROOT/place_block"

for seed in $(seq 0 499); do
  python examples/tasks_airbot_play/place_block.py \
    --data_idx "$seed" \
    --data_set_size 1 \
    --auto
done

rsync -a data/place_block/ "$DISCOVERSE_DATA_ROOT/place_block/"
```

The official script first writes the `data/place_block` in the DISCOVERSE source code directory. The last line synchronizes the actual saved round increment after passing the success condition to the large-capacity data disk. Before executing the same seed again, check whether the target round already exists to avoid duplicate generation.

Each trajectory must be checked for at least:

- The simulation success condition is true;
- The state, actions, and number of camera frames are consistent;
- The timestamp is strictly increasing;
- The padding for the final action does not span episodes;
- The replay can still complete grasping, transportation, and placement.

The `place_block` expert corpus we archived consists of 500 accepted episodes and 44,439 aligned frames.

## 4. Convert to training data

DISCOVERSE raw data typically contains `obs_action.json`, camera images or videos, and task metadata. When converted to LeRobot [robot learning data framework], unified fields are created:

```text
observation.state
observation.images.{camera}
action
task
episode_index
frame_index
timestamp
```

First convert a single trajectory, then execute in batches:

```bash
python "$EVERY_EMBODIED_ROOT/16-专题组队学习/04-AMD-ROCm策略复刻专题/code/convert_discoverse_to_lerobot.py" \
  --input-root "$DISCOVERSE_DATA_ROOT/place_block" \
  --output-root "$DATA_ROOT/discoverse-lerobot/place_block" \
  --repo-id local/discoverse-place-block \
  --task 'Place the green block in the pink bowl' \
  --fps 20 \
  --image-size 256
```

The converter reads `obs_action.json`, `cam_0.mp4`, and `cam_1.mp4` for each successful turn, and verifies that the two-channel images, 7-dimensional joint states, and 7-dimensional actions are identical per frame. DISCOVERSE records observations after executing actions, so by default `--action-bias=-1` is used, aligning the observation moment with the next action. `discoverse_conversion_manifest.json` in the conversion result records the source turn, frame number, and action index range. Do not only compare the array shape, but also replay the actions to verify the timing.

## 5. ACT Training

```bash
lerobot-train \
  --dataset.repo_id=local/discoverse-place-block \
  --dataset.root="$DATA_ROOT/discoverse-lerobot/place_block" \
  --policy.type=act \
  --policy.device=cuda \
  --policy.chunk_size=100 \
  --policy.n_action_steps=100 \
  --steps=100000 \
  --batch_size=32 \
  --save_freq=5000 \
  --log_freq=100 \
  --wandb.enable=false \
  --output_dir="$RUN_ROOT/discoverse/act_place_block"
```

On ROCm［AMD Open Compute Platform］, `--policy.device=cuda` remains the correct format. First, verify the data and backpropagation with 10–50 steps［training steps］, and then start the formal long training.

## 6. Diffusion Policy Training

```bash
lerobot-train \
  --dataset.repo_id=local/discoverse-place-block \
  --dataset.root="$DATA_ROOT/discoverse-lerobot/place_block" \
  --policy.type=diffusion \
  --policy.device=cuda \
  --steps=100000 \
  --batch_size=16 \
  --save_freq=5000 \
  --log_freq=100 \
  --wandb.enable=false \
  --output_dir="$RUN_ROOT/discoverse/diffusion_place_block"
```

The specific policy name shall be based on the `lerobot-train --help` of the installed LeRobot [robot learning data framework] version. The training configuration must include the observation mapping, action normalization, and time window.

## 7. Closed Loop Evaluation

The evaluation loop must enable the policy actions to be realistically implemented in the simulator:

```python
observation = env.reset()
for step in range(max_steps):
    action = policy.select_action(observation)
    observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
    recorder.append(observation, action, info)
    if terminated or truncated:
        break
```

Fix the two groups of seeds: train-like［training distribution similar］ and unseen［unseen distribution］, and statistically analyze proximity, grasping, lifting, transportation, alignment, and final placement. The evaluation results are written into the same round directory as the video.

## 8. Multi-perspective High-Definition Output

The `kiwi_pick.py` in MMK2 defaults to recording 3 cameras, but the resolution is 640×480. By copying the task script and only adjusting the recording resolution, the official expert state machine can be retained:

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT/DISCOVERSE"
mkdir -p "$RUN_ROOT/discoverse/mmk2_kiwi_hd"
cp examples/tasks_mmk2/kiwi_pick.py \
  "$RUN_ROOT/discoverse/mmk2_kiwi_hd/kiwi_pick_hd.py"

python - <<'PY'
import os
from pathlib import Path

path = Path(os.environ["RUN_ROOT"]) / "discoverse/mmk2_kiwi_hd/kiwi_pick_hd.py"
text = path.read_text()
text = text.replace('"width"  : 640', '"width"  : 1920')
text = text.replace('"height" : 480', '"height" : 1080')
path.write_text(text)
PY

python "$RUN_ROOT/discoverse/mmk2_kiwi_hd/kiwi_pick_hd.py" \
  --data_idx 0 \
  --data_set_size 1 \
  --auto
```

After the task is successful, the three original videos are located in `data/pick_kiwi/000/cam_0.mp4`, `cam_1.mp4`, and `cam_2.mp4`. The script only writes to disk when the success condition is met, so these videos belong to the same round as the corresponding expert actions.

Keep the original single-camera image, and generate a three-view composite version:

```bash
ffmpeg \
  -i data/pick_kiwi/000/cam_0.mp4 \
  -i data/pick_kiwi/000/cam_1.mp4 \
  -i data/pick_kiwi/000/cam_2.mp4 \
  -filter_complex '[0:v][1:v][2:v]hstack=inputs=3[v]' \
  -map '[v]' -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  "$RUN_ROOT/discoverse/mmk2_kiwi_hd/composite.mp4"
```

## 9. 3DGS Rendering

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[gs]'
hf auth login
```

Set `cfg.use_gaussian_renderer = True` in scenarios that support the Gaussian renderer, and switch the interaction window with `Ctrl+g`. Save it during verification:

- The actual loaded `.ply` point cloud path;
- Number of points and rendering resolution;
- At least one dynamic playback segment;
- A MuJoCo mesh rendering for the same task as a control.

## 10. Key Points for AMD Migration

| Module | Migration Content |
| --- | --- |
| PyTorch［Tensor computation framework］ Policy | Keep the `torch.cuda` interface, install the ROCm wheel［AMD package］ |
| MuJoCo | Output video using EGL［windowless graphics rendering interface］ |
| 3DGS［3D Gaussian splatter］ | Replace the CUDA-specific extension or use a ROCm-compilable implementation |
| Data | Correct the episode［round］ boundaries, action chunk［action block］, and camera timing |
| ACT | Keep the length of the chunk［action block］ for training and execution consistent |
| Multi-robot | Verify separately the robot MJCF, controller, and success conditions |

## 11. Result Format

The environment operation, expert success rate, and learning policy success rate are recorded separately. The example migration record includes running checks `18/18`, AIRBOT `12/12`, MMK2 `8/8`, high-definition tasks `4/4`, and 500 expert trajectories; the training model uses its own closed loop task and denominator summary.
